note: Research batch 3 (health depth) for ChatGPT to plug into data.js. Every PMID verified against the NCBI E-utilities API (titles and years match). Each study tagged with plant (oilIds), terpenes (compoundIds), uses (categories). Merge rule: skip any study whose pubmedId already exists in data.js.

studies.title: The effect of cinnamon supplementation on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: An updated systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
studies.authors: Moridpour AH, Kavyani Z, Khosravi S, et al.
studies.finding: Across 24 RCTs, cinnamon supplementation significantly reduced fasting blood sugar, HOMA-IR, and HbA1c versus control, with no significant change in serum insulin.
studies.limitations: High heterogeneity across trials; cinnamon preparations and doses varied.

studies.title: Plasma 1,8-cineole correlates with cognitive performance following exposure to rosemary essential oil aroma
studies.finding: Higher blood 1,8-cineole levels after rosemary aroma exposure correlated with better speed and accuracy on cognitive tasks, with no speed-accuracy trade-off.
studies.limitations: Correlational design, n=20, single exposure session.

studies.title: Short-term study on the effects of rosemary on cognitive function in an elderly population
studies.authors: Pengelly A, Snow J, Mills SY, et al.
studies.finding: MIXED DOSE RESPONSE: 750 mg dried rosemary leaf improved speed of memory in older adults, while 6000 mg significantly impaired cognitive performance and alertness.
studies.limitations: Dried leaf powder, not essential oil; acute single-dose effects only.

studies.title: Effect of aromatherapy on symptoms of dysmenorrhea in college students: a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial
studies.authors: Han SH, Hur MH, Buckle J, et al.
studies.journal: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
studies.finding: Topical aromatherapy with a lavender, clary sage, and rose blend significantly reduced menstrual cramp severity versus placebo.
studies.limitations: Three-oil blend tested; individual oil effects not isolated; clary sage and rose not in dataset.

studies.title: Anti-Plaque and Anti-Gingivitis Efficacy of 0.25% Lemongrass Oil and 0.2% Chlorhexidine Mouthwash in Children
studies.authors: Akula S, Nagarathna J, Srinath K
studies.finding: 0.25% lemongrass oil mouthwash reduced plaque and gingival indices in children comparably to 0.2% chlorhexidine over 21 days.
studies.limitations: n=60 children; 21-day follow-up; no adult data.

studies.title: Efficacy of cineole in patients suffering from acute bronchitis: a placebo-controlled double-blind trial
studies.finding: Cineole reduced cough frequency and bronchitis symptom scores versus placebo in a double-blind trial.
studies.limitations: Tested isolated cineole capsules, not eucalyptus oil.

studies.title: Aromatherapy for pain management in labour
studies.authors: Smith CA, Collins CT, Crowther CA
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: across 2 trials (535 women), aromatherapy showed no difference versus control for labor pain intensity, assisted vaginal birth, or caesarean section.
studies.limitations: Only 2 trials; authors concluded evidence is insufficient for practice recommendations.

studies.title: Aromatherapy with peppermint, isopropyl alcohol, or placebo is equally effective in relieving postoperative nausea
studies.finding: NULL RESULT for peppermint: nausea scores fell equally with peppermint, isopropyl alcohol, and saline placebo; authors attributed relief to controlled breathing rather than aroma.
studies.limitations: n=33; saline placebo equally effective, suggesting non-specific effects.

studies.title: Treatment of interdigital tinea pedis with 25% and 50% tea tree oil solution: a randomized, placebo-controlled, blinded study
studies.authors: Satchell AC, Saurajen A, Bell C, et al.
studies.finding: In 158 patients, tea tree oil solution improved clinical symptoms of interdigital tinea pedis versus placebo in a blinded RCT.
studies.limitations: Symptom improvement exceeded mycological cure rates.

studies.title: Concomitant therapy with Cineole (Eucalyptole) reduces exacerbations in COPD: a placebo-controlled double-blind trial
studies.authors: Worth H, Schacher C, Dethlefsen U
studies.finding: Cineole co-therapy reduced the frequency and severity of exacerbations versus placebo in COPD patients in a double-blind trial.
studies.limitations: Tested isolated cineole capsules, not eucalyptus oil; add-on to standard therapy.
